const template = `PRD TEMPLATE - STRUCTURE AND STYLE GUIDE
Use these ten sections, in this order, each exactly once.
# PRD: <short title>
## 1. Overview - one or two sentences on what is being built, taken only from the source.
## 2. Goals - stated goals only. If none are stated, say so.
## 3. User Personas - personas named in the source.
## 4. Feature List - one bullet per requirement, with its ID (R1, R2).
## 5. Acceptance Criteria - copied verbatim from the source.
## 6. Non-Functional Requirements - performance, scale, and integration requirements with exact numbers.
## 7. Stakeholders and Deadlines - names, roles, and dates.
## 8. Dependencies and Risks - dependencies, unknown ETAs, and conflicts.
## 9. Assumptions - marked Unconfirmed.
## 10. Open Questions - every ambiguity, gap, and contradiction.
Style: short declarative sentences, neutral tone, no marketing language, no invented detail.`;

const pastPrd = `PAST PRD EXAMPLE - WRITING STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, UNRELATED PRODUCT. Never reuse its content.
# PRD: Bookmarks List
## 1. Overview
Users can bookmark an item and find it again from a Bookmarks list.
## 4. Feature List
- R1: Users can bookmark an item and open it later from a Bookmarks list.
## 6. Non-Functional Requirements
- R2: Opening the Bookmarks list takes under 3 seconds.
## 10. Open Questions
- The maximum number of bookmarks per user is not specified.
Style note: each requirement is one line prefixed with its ID, and open questions are plain bullets.`;

return [
  { json: { text: template, doc_type: 'template' } },
  { json: { text: pastPrd, doc_type: 'past_prd' } }
];
